meaning: A camera that records light on a strip or sheet of light-sensitive film to make photographs.
clues: It uses light to capture a picture through a lens.
When the roll is done, the film goes to a lab or darkroom, where chemicals bring out the pictures.
You advance the film after taking a picture so the next frame is ready.
George Eastman sold a Kodak camera using film in 1889.
It has two words. The second word names a picture-making device.
assumes: A digital camera stores pictures electronically
An instant camera makes a print soon after the picture is taken
A pinhole camera has no lens

decoys.meaning: A camera that saves photos as files instead of on film.
A camera that makes a print soon after you take the picture.
A simple camera with a tiny hole instead of a lens.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Film held the scene as a real strip of pictures. A printed photo you can hold still feels special.

exchange.text: Today's version: use a phone camera and save the file.
